notes: Fifteen lists read. Main sources: SAMHSA NSDUH 2024 annual report, WHO mental disorders fact sheet (2026 update), Crisis Text Line United in Empathy 2023 issue shares, Gallup State of the World's Emotional Health 2026, Ipsos Health Service Report 2026, APA Stress in America 2025 (apa.org returned an empty page, so UPI's report of the findings is used), CDC MMWR on subjective cognitive decline. Gallup Most Important Problem names no mental-health item (only Drugs, under 1%); Ipsos What Worries the World has no mind item, so the Ipsos Health Service Report stands in. 211's snapshot names mental health and substance use as a top referral category without a count. oecd.org returned 403; OECD entries are the Subjective well-being indicators by name plus TUAC's passage on deaths of despair. Eurostat's quality-of-life page loaded but reports only life satisfaction, so it is not listed. Wikidata QIDs via wbsearchentities (rate-limited; about 30 lookups, not counted as searches). Six candidates, all with opened sources. suicidal-thoughts and self-harm should be tagged sensitive; serious-mental-illness and eating-and-body-image probably too. mental-health-care overlaps cant-get-care (Healthcare) and may belong under Body or societal Health; refine should decide. memory overlaps seeing-hearing (Senses) as an aging pain. Leads not proposed: gambling (mapped broader to drinking-too-much, whose line covers any compulsion), panic attacks and phobias (anxiety), ADHD (cant-focus), meaning in life (left to the Purpose sweep), bullying (out of scope; People, Kids or Safety).
